skill.name: writing-page-layout
skill.description: Use this skill when you need to write code for a page layout in the Next.js
skill.summary: Use this skill when you need to write code for a page layout in the Next.js
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code spans around file paths. No executable code, command invocation, prompt injection, or data-exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

static_findings.snippet: - Follow the rules below to write a page layout (`page.tsx`) in the Next.js app:
- Seperate the types and interfaces in a separate file (`srs/app/types`)

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 8 uses Markdown backticks to format the page.tsx filename in prose. The skill contains no Ruby code, shell execution, or executable script context.
Line 14 uses Markdown backticks to format a suggested types path in prose. This is documentation text and does not invoke an external command.

content.value_statement: Next.js page files can become hard to maintain when layout, types, and page logic grow together. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce modular page.tsx layouts with separated types.
actual_capabilities: Guides generation of Next.js page.tsx layout code.
Directs page layout files to stay under 40 lines.
Instructs separation of types and interfaces into a separate file.
Focuses on concise frontend page composition.
limitations: The skill is brief and does not include full layout examples.
It is specific to Next.js page layout tasks.
It does not define styling, routing, data fetching, or accessibility rules.
The suggested types path contains a typo and may need project-specific correction.

use_cases.title: Build a small app page
use_cases.description: Create a concise Next.js page layout while keeping the page file focused and modular.

use_cases.title: Refactor a long page file
use_cases.description: Move type declarations out of a crowded page layout and reduce the page file size.

use_cases.title: Standardize generated layouts
use_cases.description: Apply consistent page layout rules when generating multiple Next.js pages for a product.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Next.js page.tsx layout for a simple dashboard. Keep the page file under 40 lines and place any types in a separate types file.

prompt_templates.title: Make it modular
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a modular Next.js page.tsx for a settings page. Separate layout sections into components and keep interfaces outside the page file.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor existing layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this existing Next.js page layout to follow the skill rules. Reduce the page file to under 40 lines and move type definitions to a separate file.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a page system
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a structure for three related Next.js page layouts. Keep each page.tsx concise, define shared types separately, and explain the file organization.

output_examples.input: A request to build a dashboard page layout.
output_examples.output: A concise page layout plan with separated sections, a short page.tsx description, and a separate types file recommendation.

output_examples.input: A long page file that mixes layout and interfaces.
output_examples.output: A refactoring summary that moves interfaces out of the page file and keeps the page focused on layout composition.

output_examples.input: A request for several related app pages.
output_examples.output: A consistent file organization proposal that keeps each page compact and uses shared type definitions.

best_practices: Clarify the exact Next.js app directory path before generating files.
Keep page.tsx focused on composition and move details into components.
Review generated paths because the source skill contains a typo in the types path.
anti_patterns: Putting all layout sections, helper logic, and type definitions in one page file.
Using the 40-line limit as a reason to hide important logic in unclear abstractions.
Assuming the suggested types path is correct without checking the project structure.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps generate concise Next.js page.tsx layouts with modular structure and separated type definitions.

faq.question: Does it write full applications?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on page layout structure, not complete application architecture or backend behavior.

faq.question: Can it be used with TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions explicitly mention separating types and interfaces into a separate file.

faq.question: Does it include styling guidance?
faq.answer: No. The skill does not specify CSS, design systems, or accessibility requirements.

faq.question: Why is the 40-line rule useful?
faq.answer: It encourages page files to stay focused on layout composition instead of mixing many concerns.

faq.question: Should I use the exact types path from the skill?
faq.answer: Check your project first. The source text appears to contain a typo in the suggested path.
